precepts.text: Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow. The word of God is what really cleanses us of our sins.
precepts.point: Who did the healing? The spirit of Christ, working through Elisha. What healed Naaman was his belief and his obedience to the word of the prophet.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Naaman believed that the word of the prophet would heal him if he followed the commandment, going down to the river Jordan and dipping seven times. That belief is what healed him of his leprosy.

David prays the same way: “Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom.” Truth in the inward parts is what the Most High desires. Then: “Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.”

The water of the Jordan did not do it by itself; the Jordan was muddy water, and Naaman would rather have had the rivers of Damascus. The word of God is what really cleanses us of our sins. Naaman obeyed the word, and he was made clean, his flesh like the flesh of a little child.

precepts.text: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit and a broken and contrite heart, not so much an animal.
precepts.point: The Lord is nigh to them of a broken heart and saves such as be of a contrite spirit. Man by nature is arrogant, so the Lord has a way of breaking you down and shaming you until you say, I cannot do these things any more; I have to do better for the Lord's sake, for my own and for my people's as an example.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
David says it plainly: “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” A sacrifice for the Lord is not so much an animal. What he wants laid on the altar is a broken spirit, a broken and contrite heart, which is a broken mind.

That is the same thing Psalms 34:18 says: “The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart.” Man by nature is arrogant; we do what we want to do. So the Most High will put you in a position where he has to break you, break you down and shame you, bring you down to the lowest, until you realize: I can't do these things no more, I have to humble myself and do better, for the Lord's sake first and foremost, for my own sake, and for my people's sake as an example.

Isaiah shows where the Lord dwells when he comes near. “the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity” is the Father, and eternity is his domain, the upper room, the top floor. Yet he says, “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.” The Father and his Son deal with and dwell with the humble in spirit.

That broken spirit is the sacrifice worthy of his time. Being haughty and arrogant and offering the best sacrifices is a complete waste of time, because humility comes before honor. That is how Manasseh, a man the law said should die, found mercy: he humbled himself, and God would not despise that broken heart.

precepts.text: Saul did not listen either: to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
precepts.point: Thou desirest not sacrifice, thou delightest not in burnt offering; the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit and a contrite heart. The animals were temporary; a broken and humbled mind is the sacrifice he wants, and only then are the bullocks on the altar acceptable.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
Psalms 51:16: “For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.” David is saying, you don’t desire sacrifice, otherwise I would give it to you; you don’t care about that either. The Lord revealed to David, I don’t care about sacrifices. And Saul didn’t listen either.

“And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord?” Samuel is asking the question: does the Lord require sacrifices above obeying what he tells you to do?

“Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.” To hearken is to listen and humble yourself. That is better than the fat of rams.

So “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” The sacrifice God accepts is a broken spirit. The animals were just temporary; your mind being broken and humbled is the best sacrifice the Lord desires. You can offer and sacrifice all you want, but make sure you offer with a good heart. “Then shalt thou be pleased with the sacrifices of righteousness, with burnt offering and whole burnt offering: then shall they offer bullocks upon thine altar.” Once the sacrifices of righteousness are offered, then the bullocks on the altar become acceptable.

precepts.text: The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds, and the Lord hears it.
precepts.point: Thou desirest not sacrifice, thou delightest not in burnt offering; the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit and a contrite heart. The animals were temporary; a broken and humbled mind is the sacrifice he wants, and only then are the bullocks on the altar acceptable.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
Psalms 51:17 says “a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” Ecclesiasticus 35:17 shows what happens when the humbled one prays.

“The prayer of the humble pierceth the clouds.” It pierces the clouds: the Lord hears it. “And till it come nigh, he will not be comforted; and will not depart, till the most High shall behold to judge righteously, and execute judgment.”

That is David in Psalms 51. When Nathan confronted him after Bathsheba and Uriah, he did not stay the smartest guy in the room. He said, you are right, I am guilty: “For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.” He kept the promise he made in Psalms 32:5, “I acknowledged my sin unto thee, and mine iniquity have I not hid.” He held himself accountable, and you have to hold yourself accountable when it comes to your sins.

The bones that were broken were his humbling: being confronted with his wrong, confessing it and acknowledging it, and the consequences that followed. And out of that broken, humbled place he prayed, “Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.” That is the prayer of the humble, the one that pierces the clouds, and it is the same humility that brought mercy to King Manasseh.

precepts.text: David's repentance: I acknowledge my transgressions; against thee only have I sinned; purge me with hyssop and I shall be clean. Then will I teach transgressors thy ways. Get yourself right, then go teach the people that it is good to follow the Lord.
precepts.point: The Lord will never leave off his mercy nor abolish the posterity of his elect. He gave a remnant unto Jacob and out of him a root unto David.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Sirach says of David, “In all his works he praised the Holy One most high with words of glory; with his whole heart he sung songs, and loved him that made him.” But didn't David sin against God? He did. Yet “The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” David sinned, but David repented, and God took away his sins.

This is how he repented: “For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me. Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.” He confessed.

“Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.” And after he confessed, what did David do? “Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.” Get myself right, and then I'm going to go teach the people.

He teaches them “That all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.” Look at my example: it is good to follow the Lord, because in the end the Lord chose me as his friend.

David is a famous man, and he is an example for all of us. Some of us err in this truth, but you can recover yourself and still earn a name. You just have to do the work and be sincere. Much is given and much is required of us as leaders, so we have to be honest, confess, get clean, and then lead the people back to God.

precepts.text: Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.
precepts.point: Cast me not away from thy presence, take not thy holy spirit from me, and restore the joy of thy salvation. Then will I teach transgressors thy ways.

note.label: Pattern

precepts.why:
Solomon was knocked down, and David, the man after the Lord's own heart, was knocked down. Did they stay down? No. We are not in the business of staying down; we get knocked down and keep going. Satan tells us to stay down, and some brothers and sisters want you to stay down, but that is not what God said. “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” That is what God is looking for.

So what do we pray when Satan knocks us down? David prayed it: “Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.” We pray that the Lord does not remove his Holy Spirit from us, because that is what keeps us standing.

“Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.” You have to look at the truth with a joyful and glad heart, because you cannot live without it; it is part of your system, your life. Where else can you go? We do not give up our position; we pray that the Lord keeps strengthening us.

“Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.” When we get back up, our job is to teach, because we have been through the trial and tribulation and understand what it takes. We go right back to the business we left off, teaching our people their transgressions so they do not fall into what we fell into. Do we give that up to go sit on the couch, or sit in the back and puff up on evil?

Nobody sees the prayer, the crying at night, the tears when you are home alone thinking, I could have done better. That is the broken and contrite heart God will not despise. Tell Satan to bring it on. With a position or without it, be the same: a trooper. And when a brother is knocked down, do not applaud it; fast and pray for him, because he is still fighting the same battle you are, and your sin may just not be revealed as quickly as his.

precepts.point: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth: when you open your mouth, what comes out is supposed to be scriptural; your conversation has to be modeled after what this book says. When people leave this truth the Lord removes his words out of their mouth, and their whole conversation changes: nothing is left but slander, falsehood, strange doctrines, and flattering speech.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

That is what happens to people who leave this truth: the holy spirit goes, the Lord removes his words out of their mouth, and their whole conversation changes. Keeping the book of the law in your mouth and keeping the holy spirit go together.

precepts.text: Thou desirest not sacrifice, else would I give it: the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise. David wrote this in his repentance: the true sacrifice is being sorry and remorseful for what you did, not pleading why you were not wrong for doing wrong; that is the spirit Saul does not have.
precepts.point: Samuel makes it plain: Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams. Do you think the Lord prefers a sacrifice to atone for broken commandments over you simply keeping the commandments? That is a heavy verse.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
David wrote this in his repentance: “For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.”

The true sacrifice is being sorry and remorseful for what you did, not pleading why you were not wrong for doing wrong. That is the spirit Saul does not have.

precepts.text: David's repentance after Nathan came to him: he pleads for mercy and acknowledges his transgression.
precepts.point: Yet for David's sake the Most High gives him a lamp in Jerusalem, because David did right all his days save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite, a wrong from which David repented.

note.label: 1 Kings 15: Abijam, Asa, Nadab, and Baasha

precepts.why:
This is David’s repentance after Nathan came to him: “Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions. Wash me throughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.”

The matter of Uriah the Hittite was a real wrong, and it is the one exception the scripture names: David did right all the days of his life, “save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.” But David pleaded for mercy and acknowledged his transgression. He repented.

That is why, for David’s sake, the Most High gave Abijam a lamp in Jerusalem, even though Abijam walked in all the sins of his father and his heart was not perfect as David’s was. The children did what they saw their fathers do; David’s heart was the standard, and his repentance is part of why.

precepts.point: David asks to be washed thoroughly from his iniquity and cleansed from his sin. The question is: how are we going to be washed?

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why: David asks, “Wash me throughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.” The question is: how are we going to be washed? Psalm 119 gives the answer. “Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.” We cleanse our ways by taking heed to the word, meaning the Commandments. That is the washing David is asking for.

precepts.text: Seek the Most High with the whole heart and ask not to wander from his Commandments; in a world of evil communication we pray that he keep us on the path clean.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why: “With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments.” Cleansing comes by taking heed to the word, so we seek the Most High with the whole heart and ask him not to let us wander from his Commandments. In a world of evil communication, that is the prayer: that he keep us on the path clean. That is what it is to be washed throughly from iniquity and cleansed from sin.

precepts.text: We are made clean through the word spoken to us; when we ask to be cleansed we must stand in Christ, abiding in the word to stay on the path of righteousness.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
Christ told his disciples, “Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.” We are made clean through the word spoken to us. That lines up with Psalm 119: a young man cleanses his way by taking heed according to the word.

So when we ask, as David did, to be washed and cleansed, we must stand in Christ, abiding in the word, to stay on the path of righteousness. The word is what makes us clean.

precepts.text: There is no man that sinneth not; when Israel sins the Most High delivers them into the hand of the enemy, carried away captive.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
Solomon prayed, “If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near”. There is no man that sinneth not, and when Israel sins, the Most High delivers them into the hand of the enemy, carried away captive.

That is exactly what happened to us. A lot of people do not think we deserved to come over here on slave ships, or deserve to be shot down in the streets, or deserve the curses put on us. But we sinned against the Most High. The pants your grandma loved wearing, the auntie who thinks she can teach in the church, standing before the scriptures with a covered head, men and women with the head wrong; we set light by the Commandments as if these are small things. David says “I acknowledge my transgressions”, and that is what we must do.

precepts.text: When Israel is smitten before the enemy because they have sinned, they must turn again and confess his name.
precepts.point: The pants your grandma loved wearing, the auntie who thinks she can teach in the church, standing before the scriptures with a covered head, men and women with the head wrong; we set light by the Commandments as if these are small things. We sinned against the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“When thy people Israel be smitten down before the enemy, because they have sinned against thee, and shall turn again to thee, and confess thy name, and pray, and make supplication unto thee in this house”. Israel is smitten before the enemy because they have sinned. The way back is to turn again to the Most High and confess his name.

That is what David does in Psalm 51: “I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.” Acknowledging the sin is the first step of turning again. We were smitten down before the enemy because we sinned against the Most High, and we have to confess it the same way.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death; through sin death came into the world, and our forefathers understood this.
precepts.point: The pants your grandma loved wearing, the auntie who thinks she can teach in the church, standing before the scriptures with a covered head, men and women with the head wrong; we set light by the Commandments as if these are small things. We sinned against the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Through sin death came into the world. Our forefathers understood this. The slave ships, being shot down in the streets, the curses: these are the wages of sin, because we sinned against the Most High.

David keeps his sin ever before him because he knows what sin pays. Acknowledging our transgressions is how we turn from the wages of sin to the gift of God, eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”. In the land of our captivity we must bethink ourselves and repent, saying we have sinned, and have done perversely, and have committed wickedness.

That is David's “I acknowledge my transgressions” said as a nation. We are in the land of them that carried us captive, and there is no man that sinneth not. Instead of saying we did not deserve it, we bethink ourselves, acknowledge that we sinned against the Most High, and make supplication to him from here.

precepts.why:
“For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect?” Just because we do not believe does not make the faith of God without effect. Our unbelief does not make the Bible untrue.

David sinned against the Most High only, and he says it was “that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.” The Most High is justified whether man believes him or not. We are not going to stand before him and be justified talking about me and Jesus; his word stands, and it is our belief that has to line up with it.

We will not stand before the Most High and be justified talking about me and Jesus. Wearing pants, not wearing fringes, crossdressing: none of that will be excused. He is justified when he speaks and clear when he judges, and every man who says otherwise is a liar.

precepts.why:

So when David says “Against thee, thee only, have I sinned”, the sin is measured by the commandments. That is why wearing pants, not wearing fringes and crossdressing will not be excused: they are forbidden by the Commandments, and not knowing does not clear a man.

David says he sinned against the Most High only and did evil in his sight; the evil was a transgression of his law. Let God be true and every man a liar. The Most High is justified when he speaks and clear when he judges, because his law is the measure, and nothing done against it will be excused.

precepts.text: A clean person takes hyssop, dips it in water, and sprinkles it on the unclean; you had to be clean to do this.
precepts.point: Purge me with hyssop and I shall be clean; wash me and I shall be whiter than snow. David says this for a reason, because the ordinances set up in the earth are patterned after what goes on in the heavens, and Christ is our high priest.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
David says “Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean” for a reason. In the law, “a clean person shall take hyssop, and dip it in the water, and sprinkle it upon the tent, and upon all the vessels, and upon the persons that were there, and upon him that touched a bone, or one slain, or one dead, or a grave”. Hyssop dipped in water was sprinkled on the unclean, and you had to be clean to do it.

The ordinances set up in the earth are patterned after what goes on in the heavens, and Christ is our high priest. So David asking to be purged with hyssop is asking the clean one to sprinkle him and make him clean, so that he is washed and whiter than snow.

precepts.text: The clean person sprinkles the unclean on the third and seventh day, who then washes his clothes and is clean at evening.
precepts.point: Purge me with hyssop and I shall be clean; wash me and I shall be whiter than snow. David says this for a reason, because the ordinances set up in the earth are patterned after what goes on in the heavens, and Christ is our high priest.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“And the clean person shall sprinkle upon the unclean on the third day, and on the seventh day: and on the seventh day he shall purify himself, and wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and shall be clean at even.” The clean person sprinkles the unclean on the third day and on the seventh day, and the unclean one washes his clothes and bathes and is clean at evening.

That is the pattern behind “wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.” The ordinances in the earth are patterned after what goes on in the heavens, and Christ, our high priest, is the clean one. David wanted that purging and washing, to be clean before the Most High.

precepts.text: Let the righteous smite me, it shall be a kindness; even the bones broken by correction will rejoice because in the end you get yourself right.
precepts.point: Make me to hear joy and gladness, that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice. This does not mean the Most High literally broke his bones; it means correction.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Make me to hear joy and gladness; that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.” This does not mean the Most High literally broke David's bones; it means correction. David says the same in Psalm 141: “Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness: and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil, which shall not break my head”.

Being smitten and reproved by the righteous is a kindness and an excellent oil. Even the bones broken by correction will rejoice, because in the end you get yourself right. That is the joy and gladness David asks to hear.

precepts.text: Subdue your own understanding, reform your hearts, and you shall be kept alive and after death obtain mercy.
precepts.point: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. We must understand what we read; this is a renewing of the mind, like Nicodemus asking how a man can be born again.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.” We must understand what we read: this is a renewing of the mind, like Nicodemus asking how a man can be born again. Ezra puts it this way: “if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive and after death ye shall obtain mercy.”

A clean heart comes by subduing your own understanding and reforming your heart. The one who does that is kept alive and obtains mercy after death. That is the right spirit David asks the Most High to renew in him.

precepts.text: Be not conformed to this world but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, to prove the good and acceptable will of God.
precepts.point: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. We must understand what we read; this is a renewing of the mind, like Nicodemus asking how a man can be born again.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.” This is what David means by a clean heart and a right spirit: a renewing of the mind. It is the same thing Nicodemus was asking about when he wanted to know how a man can be born again.

You are transformed by the renewing of your mind, and by it you prove what the good and acceptable and perfect will of God is. Subdue your own understanding and reform your heart, and do not be conformed to this world.

precepts.text: Come out of her my people and be ye separate; if you do only what you want to do, you are conformed to this world and your own god.
precepts.point: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. We must understand what we read; this is a renewing of the mind, like Nicodemus asking how a man can be born again.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you”. Come out of her, my people, and be ye separate. A clean heart and a right spirit mean not being conformed to this world.

If you do only what you want to do, you are conformed to this world and to your own god. The renewing of the mind is coming out from among them and not touching the unclean thing; then the Most High receives you. That is the clean heart David prayed for.

precepts.text: The Most High returns to his place until Israel acknowledges their offense and seeks his face in their affliction.
precepts.point: Cast me not away from thy presence, and take not thy holy spirit from me. The best thing going for us is to be in the presence of the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.” The best thing going for us is to be in the presence of the Most High. Hosea shows what happens when he withdraws it: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

The Most High returns to his place until Israel acknowledges their offence and seeks his face. In our affliction we seek him early. That is why David prays not to be cast away from his presence: being out of his presence is the affliction, and acknowledging the offence is the way back into it.

precepts.text: The Most High cast down the beauty of Israel from heaven to the earth, out of rulership; we have been scattered to the four corners.
precepts.point: Cast me not away from thy presence, and take not thy holy spirit from me. The best thing going for us is to be in the presence of the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel, and remembered not his footstool in the day of his anger!” The Most High cast down the beauty of Israel from heaven to the earth, out of rulership. We have been scattered to the four corners.

That is what it looks like to be cast away from his presence. David asks the Most High not to do to him what was done to the daughter of Zion. Being in the presence of the Most High is the best thing going for us, and losing it is losing everything.

precepts.text: Set thy house in order, reprove thy people, and renounce corruption; David's house was in disarray, and the sword never left it.
precepts.point: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation and uphold me with thy free spirit. David understood the importance of losing the kingdom; from the days of John the Baptist the kingdom suffers violence, and they kill us and get away with it. That is the wages of sin.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.” David understood the importance of losing the kingdom. From the days of John the Baptist the kingdom suffers violence; they kill us and get away with it. That is the wages of sin.

Ezra was told, “Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people, comfort such of them as be in trouble, and now renounce corruption”. David's house was in disarray, and the sword never left it. Setting the house in order, reproving the people and renouncing corruption is how the joy of salvation is restored and the free spirit upholds us.

precepts.text: The Most High requires the blood of a man's life at the hand of every man's brother.
precepts.point: Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, because David had killed the man. The true baptism is not the dipping in water but the answer of a good conscience toward the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God”: David says this because he had killed the man. The Most High told Noah, “surely your blood of your lives will I require; at the hand of every beast will I require it, and at the hand of man; at the hand of every man’s brother will I require the life of man.” The Most High requires the blood of a man's life at the hand of every man's brother, so David stood guilty of blood.

The true baptism is not the dipping in water but the answer of a good conscience toward the Most High. That is what David is asking for: to be delivered from that guilt so his tongue can sing aloud of the Most High's righteousness.

precepts.text: Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed, for in the image of God made he man; David was guilty for shedding this man's blood.
precepts.point: Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, because David had killed the man. The true baptism is not the dipping in water but the answer of a good conscience toward the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.” David was guilty for shedding this man's blood, and by this word his own blood was owed. That is the bloodguiltiness he asks the God of his salvation to deliver him from.

Man is made in the image of God, so shedding his blood is required at the hand of every man's brother. David could not wash that away in water; the true baptism is the answer of a good conscience toward the Most High, and only the Most High could deliver him.

precepts.text: To obey is better than sacrifice; the Most High delights in obeying his voice more than burnt offerings.
precepts.point: For thou desirest not sacrifice, else would I give it; thou delightest not in burnt offerings. Christ left us his example and taught nothing different than David.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.” Samuel said the same to Saul: “Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.” The Most High delights in obeying his voice more than in burnt offerings.

David knew that, and Christ left us his example and taught nothing different than David. To obey is better than sacrifice.

precepts.text: He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough.
precepts.point: For thou desirest not sacrifice, else would I give it; thou delightest not in burnt offerings. Christ left us his example and taught nothing different than David.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why: “He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.” Keeping the law is offerings enough. The Most High does not desire sacrifice or delight in burnt offering; what he wants is the man who keeps his law. That is the offering David knew to bring, and Christ taught nothing different.

precepts.text: He that taketh heed to the Commandments offereth a peace offering.
precepts.point: For thou desirest not sacrifice, else would I give it; thou delightest not in burnt offerings. Christ left us his example and taught nothing different than David.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why: “He that requiteth a good turn offereth fine flour; and he that giveth alms sacrificeth praise.” Read with the verse before it: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering, and he that requites a good turn and gives alms is bringing fine flour and a sacrifice of praise. Those are the sacrifices the Most High wants, not the burnt offering David says he delights not in. Obedience and doing good to your brother are the offering.

precepts.text: To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Most High; when you leave sin and repent that is your offering.
precepts.point: For thou desirest not sacrifice, else would I give it; thou delightest not in burnt offerings. Christ left us his example and taught nothing different than David.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord; and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.” When you leave sin and repent, that is your offering. Forsaking unrighteousness is the propitiation.

That is why David could say the Most High desires not sacrifice. What pleases him is a man departing from wickedness, which is what David is doing in this whole psalm. Christ left us his example and taught nothing different.

precepts.text: Sacrifice, offerings, and burnt offerings the Most High would not; he desires obedience.
precepts.point: For thou desirest not sacrifice, else would I give it; thou delightest not in burnt offerings. Christ left us his example and taught nothing different than David.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law”. Sacrifice, offerings and burnt offerings the Most High would not; he had no pleasure in them. He desires obedience.

This is the same thing David said: “thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.” Samuel said to obey is better than sacrifice, and Ecclesiasticus says he that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough. Christ left us his example and taught nothing different than David.

precepts.text: Go on with thy business in meekness; the greater thou art, the more humble thyself and find favor before the Most High.
precepts.point: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit, a broken and a contrite heart, which the Most High will not despise. Contrite means meek and teachable.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” Contrite means meek and teachable. “My son, go on with thy business in meekness; so shalt thou be beloved of him that is approved.” The greater thou art, the more humble thyself, and thou shalt find favour before the Most High.

That meekness is the contrite heart. It is the sacrifice the Most High will not despise, and it makes you beloved.

precepts.text: Mysteries are revealed unto the meek.
precepts.point: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit, a broken and a contrite heart, which the Most High will not despise. Contrite means meek and teachable.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why: “Many are in high place, and of renown: but mysteries are revealed unto the meek.” Not to the high and renowned, but to the meek. A contrite heart is meek and teachable, and that is the heart the Most High reveals his mysteries to. That is why a broken and a contrite heart is the sacrifice he will not despise.

precepts.text: For the power of the Lord is great, and he is honored of the lowly.
precepts.point: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit, a broken and a contrite heart, which the Most High will not despise. Contrite means meek and teachable.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why: “For the power of the Lord is great, and he is honoured of the lowly.” The Most High is honoured by the lowly. A broken spirit and a contrite heart, meek and teachable, is what honours him, and that is the sacrifice of God he will not despise. The high and renowned do not honour him; the lowly do, and mysteries are revealed to them.

precepts.text: Make me to hear joy and gladness, that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.
precepts.point: He asks that His work appear unto His servants and His glory unto their children, that the beauty of the Lord our God be upon us, and that He establish the work of our hands. The Lord will give us according to the fruit of our doings.

note.label: Psalm 90: Teach Us to Number Our Days

precepts.why:
Moses prays, “O satisfy us early with thy mercy; that we may rejoice and be glad all our days. Make us glad according to the days wherein thou hast afflicted us, and the years wherein we have seen evil.” David prays the same after his own affliction: “Make me to hear joy and gladness; that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.”

The bones the Most High has broken are the days wherein he afflicted us and the years wherein we have seen evil. The prayer is that the gladness match the affliction, that the broken bones themselves rejoice. Satisfy us early with mercy, and let the same hand that broke us make us glad.

precepts.text: Purge me and I shall be clean, wash me and I shall be whiter than snow, showing white in the scriptures means made clean and undefiled.
precepts.point: His head is as the most fine gold, and his locks are bushy and black as a raven; this is the same as reading of the Christ having woolly hair and the Most High having hair of pure wool.

note.label: Song of Solomon 5: My Beloved Is White and Ruddy

precepts.why:
“My beloved is white and ruddy”: Christianity argues these verses prove the beloved is a white man, but white in the scriptures does not mean white skin. “Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.”

David is not asking for a change of skin. White means undefiled and unspotted, clean and clear, made clean. There is nobody who is literally white; the beloved is white in the sense David means here.

points: David says, "I acknowledge my transgressions, and my sin is ever before me." That is something we must do: acknowledge our transgressions.
A lot of people do not think we deserve to come over here on slave ships or deserve to be shot down in the streets or deserve the curses put on us. But we sinned against the Most High.

The pants your grandma loved wearing, the auntie who thinks she can teach in the church, standing before the scriptures with a covered head, men and women with the head wrong; we set light by the Commandments as if these are small things. We sinned against the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

points: Against the Most High only has David sinned and done this evil in his sight, that the Most High might be justified when he speaks and clear when he judges.

We are not going to stand before the Most High and be justified talking about "me and Jesus." If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God. Wearing pants, not wearing fringes, crossdressing; none of that will be excused.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

points: David was shapen in iniquity, and in sin did his mother conceive him, meaning he was born from a natural childbirth.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

points: The Most High desires truth in the inward parts, and in the hidden part he makes us to know wisdom.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

points: Purge me with hyssop and I shall be clean; wash me and I shall be whiter than snow. David says this for a reason, because the ordinances set up in the earth are patterned after what goes on in the heavens, and Christ is our high priest.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

points: Make me to hear joy and gladness, that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice. This does not mean the Most High literally broke his bones; it means correction.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

points: Hide thy face from my sins and blot out all my iniquities. Blessed is the man whose transgressions are covered.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

points: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. We must understand what we read; this is a renewing of the mind, like Nicodemus asking how a man can be born again.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

points: Cast me not away from thy presence, and take not thy holy spirit from me. The best thing going for us is to be in the presence of the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

points: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation and uphold me with thy free spirit. David understood the importance of losing the kingdom; from the days of John the Baptist the kingdom suffers violence, and they kill us and get away with it. That is the wages of sin.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

points: Then will I teach transgressors thy ways, and sinners shall be converted unto thee.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

points: Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, because David had killed the man. The true baptism is not the dipping in water but the answer of a good conscience toward the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

points: O Lord, open thou my lips, and my mouth shall show forth thy praise.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

points: For thou desirest not sacrifice, else would I give it; thou delightest not in burnt offerings. Christ left us his example and taught nothing different than David.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

points: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit, a broken and a contrite heart, which the Most High will not despise. Contrite means meek and teachable.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

points: Do good in thy good pleasure unto Zion; build thou the walls of Jerusalem. In captivity we are like those who built the wall with one hand and fought with the other; it is time to rebuild a nation.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed
